title: Genesis, looking back
hookLine: a garden, a rainbow, a ladder, a wrestling match, a brother forgiven
tomorrow: when Moses left Egypt, whose bones did he carry?

lines: A REJECTION, A FIGHT, A LATE APOLOGY.
cards: A rejection email that pushed someone toward the work they love. A fight that ended a friendship, and the apology years later that started a better one. People tell these stories carefully, because the hurt was real.
Genesis ends on one. Their father has just died, and the brothers are afraid. Years ago they threw their younger brother into a pit and sold him.
Now he rules in Egypt, and holds their lives in his hands.

teach.b: Joseph answers: “Fear not: for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.” Notice the order.
He names the evil first. He doesn't call harm good. He sets something larger beside it.

teach.h: A GARDEN, A BOW, A LADDER.
teach.b: Look back over Genesis and that pattern keeps surfacing: a garden lost, and God still calling, “Where art thou?”; a flood, then a bow in the cloud, “a token of a covenant between me and the earth”; a runaway on a stone pillow who wakes and says, “Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not.”
Jews read these stories as Torah, Christians as the opening of their Bible. Now a neighbor. Muslims know this brother as Yusuf, and the Qur'an tells his story in the surah named for him.

teach.h: A NEIGHBOR: HAVE NO FEAR THIS DAY.
teach.b: When his brothers stand before him at last, he says: “Have no fear this day! May Allah forgive you.”
Here's one to tell a friend: in both books, the wronged brother's first words to the frightened ones are nearly the same, fear not.
Shared ground: a brother who has the power to take revenge, and won't.
An honest difference: the Qur'an honors Yusuf as a prophet, and its telling keeps turning to what God knows and plans; Genesis tells him as one son in a long, tangled family story.

how: Christians read Genesis in worship and at home, and its stories of Noah, Jacob and Joseph are among the Bible stories many children hear early on.

o: the book of laws Moses gave on Sinai
the first book, from a garden to forgiveness
a list of family trees kept by the priests

p: the LORD is in this place

s: Joseph tells his brothers that what they did wasn't really wrong
he names it first: ye thought evil against me. then: God meant it unto good.
in Genesis 50, Joseph's first words to his frightened brothers are 'Fear not'
fear not: for am I in the place of God?
the Qur'an has a surah named for Joseph
Surah Yusuf, where he tells his brothers, have no fear this day.

games.q: your Muslim friend says, "Yusuf is my favorite story in the Qur'an." you know Joseph from Genesis. what's a fair reply?
o: "Genesis and the Qur'an tell his story with exactly the same details, start to end."
"same forgiving brother, same fear not. the Qur'an calls him a prophet; Genesis, one son in a family."
"it's really the same book, just under a different name and in another language."
games.why: shared ground: a wronged brother who won't take revenge, and nearly the same first words. an honest difference, ranking neither: how each book frames him.

practice: Walk slowly for about a minute, around a room or down a hallway. Every few steps, let one Genesis picture pass: a garden, a rainbow, a ladder, a wrestling match, a brother forgiven. Notice where you stop; that may be your story.
If you pray, sit afterward and pray from inside it.

wordCard.voice: Genesis. The Bible's first book: a garden, a rainbow, a ladder, a wrestling match, and a brother who names the harm and forgives.

carryVoice: Keep this: meant for good, with the harm named and the good set beside it. See you tomorrow.
